Definition: to clap the hands (in token of compact, derision, grief, indignation, or punishment); by implication of satisfaction, to be enough; by implication of excess, to vomit
BiblicalUsage: çâphaq means to clap the hands, in compact, derision, grief, or satisfaction, and the Bible means it plainly. It occurs 10 times in the Old Testament, in 1 Kings and Ezekiel and elsewhere, and none of those places bends the word out of shape. What it says in one place is what it says in all of them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe çâphaq earns its place. To clap the hands, in compact, derision, grief, or satisfaction is the kind of thing God repeats because His people need to hear it more than once.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
